images.seen: Matches Cliopatria for Egypt, Hittites, Mitanni, Assyria, Babylonia, Elam and Mycenaean Greece; the dossiers add Qatna, Ugarit, Kizzuwatna, Alashiya, Arzawa, Isuwa, Hayasa-Azzi and Kaska (contested) sensibly; Egypt's Levant is in the vassal tint.

The Jan-1 anchor leaves 161 Khuzestan cells to nobody between Babylonia and Elam; the elam_-1400 keyframe fills them at -1400 (the elam snap), a seam artefact of the neighbour window's narrower Elam shape; Susa was Elamite throughout per the dossier.

Hittites hold Syria down to Homs with Amurru, Ugarit, Carchemish, Isuwa and Hayasa-Azzi as vassals; Arzawa contested; but Assyria held the whole Khabur Valley (Hasaka) since -1363, against the Mitanni page; patched.
Shang matches Cliopatria; the dossier cultures (Indus Valley, Malwa, Jorwe, Southern Neolithic ashmound, Kashi, Sanxingdui, Jomon) sit where the pages put them; nothing wrong seen.

Before the patch: Assyria wraps the Khabur and middle Euphrates, Mitanni is a western rump; Egypt's Levant is mostly direct with 43 vassal cells and about 60 Egyptian cells round Damascus; a detached 3-cell Assyria speckle in the Syrian steppe.
Mitanni holds the Khabur heartland round Washukanni; Canaan is in the Egyptian vassal tint; Assyria keeps the Tigris lands and the middle Euphrates.
The Khabur part of the Mitanni rump now takes the Hittite-vassal tint with the rest (events 2-3), Carchemish stays a vassal inside it.

Mitanni rump = Euphrates bend plus Khabur Valley; the Hittites hold the Gaziantep-Adiyaman lands west of the Euphrates; Egypt holds Canaan as vassal tint only; Damascus and the Syrian steppe are nobody's. Remaining speckles: 3 Assyria cells in the steppe and 4 north of Hasaka.

issues.what: Khabur Valley (Hasaka, 82 cells, Washukanni) drawn as Assyrian from -1363. The region 'Assyria' of assyria ledger 14 sweeps in Hasaka, and mitanni ledger 5 sends it to Assyria again at -1350, while the page says the kingdom 'had by now been reduced to the Khabur Valley' and Washukanni and the Khabur cities fall under Wasashatta (c. 1285-1265); Ashur-uballit I's annexation names no region.
The Khabur part of the rump was drawn direct while the rest of Mitanni carried the Hittite-vassal tint (Shattiwaza, c. 1330-1305).

Keyframes with no 'to': mitanni_-1400 (note: valid -1400..-1351) and new-kingdom-of-egypt_-1400 (note: valid -1447..-1353) run to Cliopatria's -1301 and are unioned with the later keyframes, so Mitanni claimed its whole 1400 shape and Egypt kept claiming Syria north of Canaan in every year to -1301. Effects: 912 cell-years of assyria/mitanni R2 conflicts, hittites/mitanni R2, Egypt-Hittite, -Amurru and -Ugarit conflicts, the Egypt -1352 snap (225 cells) and the Mitanni -1345 snap (44 cells) all arose from it; about 60 cells round Damascus and the steppe stayed Egyptian to -1301. Conflicts go from 1308 to 241 cell-years and snaps from 7 to 5.

hittites_-1345 holds the 1400 shape plus the part of the 1300 shape inside the Levant region, so it released about 50 cells of Gaziantep, Adiyaman and Kilis that hittites ledger 4 had just taken from Mitanni (west of the Euphrates); once Mitanni's stale 1400 claim was cut they would have become nobody's.
Canaan drawn as direct Egyptian land from -1352 (only 43 vassal cells left) although the keyframe note says 'as vassal tint' and the Amarna letters show Canaanite rulers as Egyptian vassals to 1332.

Elam keyframe snap at -1400 (128 cells, Khuzestan): the 1 January anchor leaves the Khuzestan lowlands to nobody, because the neighbour window's elam_-1600 shape is narrower; the elam_-1400 keyframe is marked ok and Susa is the capital throughout.

Babylonia occupies Khuzestan twice (-1350 Kurigalzu I, -1320 Kurigalzu II), one year each; the Kassites page and the Elam page give the two dates, and the Kurigalzu II page says the conquest 'now tends to be assigned to the earlier king'.
Qatna ends -1337 (palace destroyed 1340 per its page) while the Mitanni page lists Qatna among the lands Suppiluliuma subjugated in 1345; the dossier's -1337 is a reasoned bridge.

Size-rule conflicts: hayasa-azzi/kaska (Gumushane, Bayburt), jorwe/southern-neolithic-ashmound, mycenae/mycenaean-greece, ugarit/amurru/qatna vs Egypt or Mitanni: the smaller state won, as the dossiers' own regions say.
Contests still open at the end: arzawa/hittites (-1320, ends -1300 with the dossier's own contest_end and dissolve) and kaska/hittites (-1430 to -1112): both follow dossier events.

Small leftovers of mitanni ledger 5's region (Mitanni-1400 minus the 1300 shape and the Hittite shape): 3 detached Assyria cells in the Syrian steppe (34.8-35.0 N, 37.6-37.8 E) and 4 cells north of Hasaka (36.9-37.2 N, 40.5-41.6 E); the middle-Euphrates Dayr az-Zawr lands (about 80 cells) also go to Assyria at -1350 although the page names no region.

colour_clashes.note: OKLab 0.060 from the packet; Carchemish is a Hittite vassal drawn inside Hittite land, so the two are hard to tell apart.
Qatna's own tan looks the same as Egypt's vassal tint, and Qatna borders Egyptian Canaan; Qatna is Egypt's vassal until -1337, so it reads right but cannot be told from the Canaanite vassal land.

problems: next window: new-kingdom-of-egypt_-1300 and _-1240 have verdict 'wrong' but a Cliopatria-shape correction, which the compiler treats as a claim; with Egypt's stale -1400 claim cut at -1353, the -1300 keyframe will take Syria north of Canaan back for Egypt at -1300 (Hittites win the overlaps by size). The m1300-m1201 agent should override both with a Canaan-only region.

next window: the Khabur Valley now stays Mitanni's to -1301, so assyria ledger 15 and mitanni ledgers 11-12 (-1300, Hasaka and Washukanni) will move 82 cells in -1300 instead of being no-ops; the end anchor m1300 differs from the published one in 185 cells (82 Hasaka to Mitanni, 59 Syrian cells from Egypt to nobody, 43 Gaziantep-Adiyaman cells from Mitanni to the Hittites, 1 to nobody) and 151 cells of status.
hierarchy: no rows of data/hierarchy.csv overlap -1400..-1301; nothing to fix.
events/4 uses the counterpart 'canaanite-city-states', which has no dossier (as the dossier's own ledger 5 does); check-patch notes it, the trial applies it.
